summary: Iteration 5 — Tested all 4 new study features (manual edits, PDF export, bookmarks, SM-2 flashcards) + dispatcher (Mongo/SQL). 34/36 tests pass. Found 1 CRITICAL bug: GET /api/lectures/{id}/pdf always returns 500 because filename in Content-Disposition contains em-dash (—) which Starlette cannot encode as latin-1 HTTP header. Affects 100% of PDF downloads regardless of lecture content.

critical.issue: Returns 500 UnicodeEncodeError: 'latin-1' codec can't encode character '\u2014'. Root cause: routes/study.py line 86 builds filename as `f"{lecture.title[:60].replace('/', '_')} — Notes.pdf"` — the literal em-dash (—) in the f-string violates latin-1 used by HTTP headers in Starlette. Fix: replace the literal em-dash with a plain hyphen '-' (ASCII) OR use RFC 5987 encoding: `headers={'Content-Disposition': f"attachment; filename*=UTF-8''{urllib.parse.quote(filename)}"}`.

After fix, re-run tests/test_study.py::TestPdfExport to verify.

rca_of_the_issue: RCA — PDF 500 error: routes/study.py builds f-string `f"{title[:60].replace('/', '_')} — Notes.pdf"` containing literal em-dash (U+2014). Starlette's StreamingResponse encodes headers as latin-1 (per HTTP RFC 7230 historical default in the library). latin-1 cannot encode U+2014, so the response init raises UnicodeEncodeError -> uvicorn returns 500. Reproduction: any GET /api/lectures/{ready_id}/pdf with valid auth. Mitigation: replace em-dash with hyphen (one-character change) OR use RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''...` with urllib.parse.quote. PDF bytes themselves are well-formed (TestPdfUnit decodes the bytes via pypdf and finds the title + all section headings).
